q: 1. The specific gravity of sand is approximately
explain: Sand is composed mainly of quartz, whose specific gravity is close to 2.65, commonly rounded to about 2.6.

q: 2. Shaking test is also called as .............
explain: The shaking test and dilatancy test refer to the same field identification procedure.

q: 3. Soils containing organic matters
options: shrink with increase of moisture content
explain: Organic soils (peats etc.) have a fibrous, porous, spongy texture due to decomposed plant matter, giving low bearing capacity and high compressibility.

q: 4. Which of the following clay mineral gives maximum swelling?
explain: Montmorillonite has an expansive lattice structure, giving it the highest swelling potential among common clay minerals.

q: 5. Stoke's law is used to determine the .............
options: grain size distribution of those soils whose grain size is finer than 0.075 mm
explain: Stoke's Law is applied in sedimentation (hydrometer) analysis to determine the grain size distribution of fine particles finer than 0.075 mm.

q: 6. According to Stoke's law, the velocity at which grains settle out of suspension, all other factors being equal, is dependent upon .............
explain: Stoke's Law settling velocity depends on grain shape, weight (density), and size together.

q: 7. Sieving is not practicable for grain sizes smaller than about .............
explain: Below about 0.075 mm, particles are too fine for mechanical sieving and sedimentation (hydrometer) analysis is used instead.

q: 8. The liquidity index is given as .............
explain: Liquidity Index (LI) = (natural water content - plastic limit) / plasticity index.

q: 9. Thixotropy of soils refers to .............
options: gain of strength of soil with passage of time after it has been remoulded
loss of strength of soil with passage of time after it had been remoulded
thickening of soil with particles with water
explain: Thixotropy is the phenomenon of a remoulded soil gradually regaining strength over time without any change in water content.

q: 10. The compressibility of the following soil is somewhat less .............
explain: Among these organic/inorganic clays and silts of varying plasticity, OL (low plasticity organic clay) has comparatively lower compressibility.

q: 11. The workability of the following soil is better .............
explain: Being lower plasticity, OL soil is comparatively easier to work with as a construction material than the higher-plasticity options.

q: 12. Soil in which some of the intermediate size particles are missing is known as .............
explain: A gradation curve missing some intermediate particle sizes (a gap-graded curve) defines a skip graded soil.

q: 13. Toughness test is also called as .............
explain: The toughness test, which assesses the firmness of a soil pat at plastic limit, is also known as the rolling test.

q: 14. The liquidity index of soil is given by
explain: Liquidity index (Il) is calculated as the natural water content minus the plastic limit, divided by the plasticity index.

q: 15. In the modified proctor test the drop height of the rammer is .............
explain: The Modified Proctor test uses a heavier rammer dropped from 45 cm, giving higher compactive effort than the Standard Proctor test.

q: 16. Stoke's law is applicable to particles upto ............. effective diameter.
explain: Stoke's Law is valid for fine particles up to about 0.2 mm, but sedimentation analysis specifically applies it for particles as fine as around 0.002 mm.

q: 17. Which of the following is a cohesion less soil?
explain: Sand particles lack the electrochemical bonding of clay minerals, making sand a cohesionless soil.

q: 18. Finest grain particles are contained in .............
explain: Clay has the smallest particle size among these soil types, generally below 0.002 mm.

q: 19. Clays containing organic matter are made suitable for stabilization, by first adding a percentage of .............
explain: Per the reference key, resins are used as the initial additive to counteract organic matter before further stabilization of such clays.

q: 20. The unconfined compressive strength of a hard clay is .............
explain: Hard clay has the highest consistency and unconfined compressive strength, typically above 400 kN/m2.

q: 21. Soil can exist in
explain: Depending on saturation, soil can be single-phase (dry, solids only), two-phase (fully saturated: solids+water, or dry: solids+air), or three-phase (partially saturated), so all conditions are possible.

q: 22. The shape of plot between shear and normal stresses according to Mohr's theory is .............
explain: Mohr's failure envelope is generally a curve, though it is often approximated as a straight line (Mohr-Coulomb) over limited stress ranges.

q: 23. The workability of the following soil will be excellent as a construction material .............
explain: Well-graded gravel (GW) has excellent grading and drainage properties, making it an excellent construction material.

q: 24. Sensitivity of a soil can be defined as
options: Percentage of volume change of soil under saturated condition
Ratio of compressive strength of unconfined undisturbed soil to that of soil in a remolded state
Ratio of volume of voids to volume to solids
explain: Sensitivity St = (unconfined compressive strength, undisturbed) / (unconfined compressive strength, remoulded at same water content), indicating strength loss upon remoulding.

q: 25. The soil sample for the hydrometer analysis is pretreated with the following agent .............
explain: Hydrogen peroxide (an oxidising agent) is used to remove organic matter from the soil sample before hydrometer analysis.

q: 26. According to IS code, the permissible values of total settlements of rafts on clays and sands are .............
explain: For raft foundations, IS code permits larger total settlement: 100 mm on clay and 65 mm on sand.
This is the standard formula for coefficient of curvature (Cc), used alongside Cu to assess grading.

q: 28. The symbol SP indicates .............
explain: In USCS notation, SP denotes poorly graded sand.

q: 29. Plasticity needle is used to determine
options: Plastic limit of the soil used in compaction
Penetration resistance to control field compaction
Penetration value of bitumen used in road construction
Swelling index of black cotton soils
explain: The plasticity/proctor needle is a field device used to measure penetration resistance, helping control and verify field compaction quality against the laboratory compaction curve.

q: 30. Bitumen, when added to soil, mainly
explain: Bitumen stabilization primarily works by coating soil particles to reduce water absorption and infiltration, essentially acting as a waterproofing/binding agent.

q: 31. Hydroscopic water can be removed in the lab. by oven-drying at a temp. of .............
explain: Standard oven drying at 105-110°C is sufficient to remove hygroscopic moisture from soil samples.

q: 32. In which type of soil the cohesive force is assumed to be zero
explain: Sandy (granular) soils lack significant inter-particle attraction, so cohesion is taken as zero (c=0) in strength analysis, unlike clayey soils.

q: 33. Two soils A and B are having a flow index of 9 and 6 respectively. Then which soil has a better strength as function of WC .............
explain: A lower flow index indicates a steeper strength-loss curve with moisture change, meaning soil B (flow index 6) retains strength better with changing water content.

q: 34. Specific surface of the following soil is more .............
explain: Clay particles are the smallest and most plate-like, giving them by far the highest specific surface area.

q: 35. The unconfined compression test can be conducted on .............
explain: Because it relies on the specimen standing unconfined, the unconfined compression test only works on cohesive (clayey) soils that can self-support.

q: 36. The assumption in sedimentation analysis is as follows .............
options: particles settle independent of other particles
walls of the jar where in settlement analysis is done do not affect the settlement
explain: Sedimentation analysis relies on all these idealizing assumptions together: spherical particles, independent settling, and negligible jar-wall effects.

q: 37. A soil is in a semi-solid state, if the consistency index is .............
explain: A consistency index greater than 1 (natural water content below plastic limit) places the soil in the semi-solid to solid state.

q: 38. With the increase of deflocculating agent, the density of soil suspension will .............
explain: Excess dispersing agent adds dissolved solids that lower the relative density reading compared to a plain water blank, requiring correction.

q: 39. Minimum size of the particles of silt soil is
explain: Silt particles range from about 0.002 mm (the upper limit of clay) up to about 0.075 mm, so the minimum size of a silt particle corresponds to 0.002 mm, bordering the clay fraction.

q: 40. In a soil if the water content is equal to the liquid limit, its relative consistency is .............
explain: Relative (liquidity) consistency of 0 occurs when natural water content equals the liquid limit, i.e., soil is at the liquid limit boundary.

q: 41. For a well graded soil the co-efficient of curvature will be between .............
explain: A well-graded soil requires a coefficient of curvature (Cc) between 1 and 3, per standard classification criteria.

q: 42. The stress-strain curve of an over consolidated clay is similar to that of .............
explain: Over-consolidated clay shows peak-strength, dilative behaviour under shear similar to dense sand.

q: 43. The shrinkage index is equal to .............
explain: Per the reference key, shrinkage index is expressed as liquid limit minus shrinkage limit in this classification.

q: 44. The ratio of the liquid limit minus the natural content of a soil to its plasticity index, is known as .............
explain: This ratio, (LL - w)/PI, defines relative consistency (also related to consistency index).

q: 45. Bentonite contains predominantly .............
explain: Bentonite is a clay predominantly composed of montmorillonite, giving it its characteristic high swelling capacity.

options: soil composed of two different soils
fine grained soil with little or no plasticity
clay with a high percentage of the clay mineral
explain: Silt is defined as a fine-grained soil that exhibits little to no plasticity, distinguishing it from clay.

q: 47. The symbol CL indicates .............
explain: In USCS notation, CL denotes inorganic clay of low to medium plasticity.
